source-integrity.provenance: issuer financial and operating disclosures plus independent valuation context; Beta/Resolver causal lineage retained
source-integrity.freshness: Q2 issuer evidence August 2026; ratepayer/load evidence July 2026; independent valuation September 2026
source-integrity.duplicateOriginCollapse: duplicate Q2 issuer origin collapsed; derived Beta/Resolver evidence not treated as independent primary sourcing
source-integrity.sourceIndependence: issuer facts separated from independent valuation interpretation
source-integrity.rawDerivedConsistency: strong earnings/load-growth narrative is retained alongside nearly flat quarterly revenue; no inference that forecast load already equals realized revenue

company-underwriting.financialOperatingTrajectory: Regulated earnings growth and utility investment remain constructive, while quarterly revenue growth was nearly flat and forward large-load economics depend on rate recovery.
company-underwriting.balanceSheet: Capital-intensive generation/grid build requires continued financing and regulatory recovery; regulated cash-flow model provides resilience but does not eliminate leverage/capex risk.
company-underwriting.customersContracts: Large-load/data-center demand is a credible growth vector, but the committed-versus-prospective split is incompletely disclosed in current evidence.
company-underwriting.governanceCapitalAllocation: Long operating history and regulated capital deployment support stewardship; affordability and recovery discipline remain key tests.
company-underwriting.pricingPowerConcentration: Regulated rate mechanisms provide structured cost recovery rather than unconstrained pricing; customer affordability and commission approval constrain economics.
company-underwriting.catalysts: Large-load conversion, grid/generation investment and nuclear baseload utilization; realization timing remains conditional.

thesisQuality.basis: Regulated utility demand, firm generation/grid assets and earnings growth support durable value capture, while load conversion and recovery remain conditional.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Earnings growth and investment/customer growth are constructive, but nearly flat quarterly revenue and capital intensity temper momentum quality.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Independent September valuation commentary characterized SO as relatively low-valued within utilities with 6-8% expected EPS growth, supporting moderate headroom rather than exceptional asymmetry.

catalystScore.basis: Large-load growth, regulated investment and baseload utilization are identifiable multi-year catalysts, with timing dependent on contracts and approvals.

governancePower.basis: Long-duration regulated execution and explicit customer-affordability commitments support stewardship, with recovery discipline still material.

alignment2036.basis: Electricity, grid capacity and firm nuclear generation are foundational infrastructure for multiple electrification and compute-demand futures.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Generation, transmission/distribution and customer growth create multiple linked regulated demand engines across operating utilities.

bottleneckControl.basis: Owned regulated generation/grid assets and nuclear baseload control scarce interconnection and firm-power capacity, subject to regulatory constraints.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Baseline regulated demand is resilient across scenarios while incremental data-center/electrification load adds upside without being required for utility survival.

substitutionResilience.basis: Grid and firm-generation infrastructure have high replacement friction, though customer-side generation and alternative suppliers constrain monopoly-like assumptions.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Diversified utility asset base and mature operating infrastructure support resilience, while large-build equipment/fuel/capex dependencies remain.

pricingPower.basis: Regulated recovery mechanisms can preserve economics, but commission oversight and affordability commitments constrain discretionary pricing.

riskEvidence.basis: Capital intensity, regulatory recovery, affordability and forecast-load conversion are meaningful but moderated by regulated baseline demand and established assets.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current primary financial/operating evidence and independent valuation context support scoring; project-specific contracted-load economics remain incompletely disclosed.

scoreRecord.thesis: Southern owns regulated grid and firm-generation infrastructure positioned for durable electricity demand and large-load growth, with returns conditioned by disciplined capex and regulatory recovery.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Forecast large loads may arrive slower than capital deployment or regulators may constrain recovery to protect affordability.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Conversion of large-load forecasts into contracted/energized demand and approved recovery-backed grid/generation investment.

contradictions.claim: Historic load-growth narrative versus nearly flat quarterly operating revenue.
contradictions.resolution: Regulated earnings and load timing can diverge from quarterly revenue; retain as timing/economics test rather than current falsification.

unknowns.item: Exact committed-versus-prospective large-load split and project-specific allowed-return economics remain incomplete.
